narrative.overview:
Pitchy reads like a Metro Manila train line board. Each weather source is a line with its own fixed colour; its state is the stop, and its "current until" time reads like the next departure. A Midnight Navy shell (top bar, navigation rail, kickoff strip) frames a near-white work ground where flat, hairline-bordered cards carry the data. The board is built to be scanned at a glance, one-handed, in sun and glare: big tabular figures, an icon and a word on every state, and nothing that fades away when it gets old. Stale data stays on the board and gets a dashed stamp.

The components are standard Material 3 on purpose. The world comes in through the palette, the type weights, the density and one signature component, the source rail. Android and Windows get the same look because every font is bundled with the app and there are no per-platform styles. Colour is split into two layers that never mix. The themed layer (shell, ground, ink, accent) changes with Light, Dark, Pitch Green or Custom. The fixed layer (data-state colours and the safety ramp) means the same thing in every theme.

The system rejects the usual weather-app look of a hero temperature over a grid of identical tonal cards. Values sit in a small 2x2 grid (4 columns on wide windows) under the source rail. Each value is one tap from its proof: the source, fetch and validity times, and the spread across sources.

The board refinement kept this world and changed its material: Midnight Navy and Glacier, Switzer for all UI, IBM Plex Mono for Line Board figures only, one overlay shadow and one motion language. Brand and product are separate: the landing page's Racing Red never enters the app.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight Navy shell around a cool near-white ground. The board is flat; only overlays cast one navy-tinted shadow.
One fixed, cool line colour per weather source, used for its rail dot, validity bar and the dot on its value card.
Every data state is a pill with an icon and an uppercase word. Stale also gets a dashed outline.
Switzer for all UI (default figures are tabular); IBM Plex Mono only for Line Board figures.
Fixed safety and state colours sit outside every theme; one icon per hazard level.
Motion is rare and short: overlays, expand and collapse, the new chat reply, the Updating spinner and press feedback.

rules.name: The Two Layers Rule
rules.body: Themes change only shell, ground, surface, hairline, ink and accent. Data-state colours and the safety ramp are fixed in every theme and never take a custom colour.

rules.name: The Custom Two Rule
rules.body: Custom changes only the shell and the accent, and both come from the eight fixed swatches. Every swatch passes 4.5:1 against white, and none is red, orange or yellow, so a themed colour can never pass for a safety colour.

rules.name: The Cool Lines Rule
rules.body: Source line colours are cool hues only. The safety ramp (yellow, orange, red) is never used as a line colour or as decoration.

rules.name: The Icon and Word Rule
rules.body: No state is shown by colour alone. Every state shows an icon and a word, and Stale also gets a dashed outline, so it still reads in greyscale.

rules.name: The Hazard Severity Rule
rules.body: A hazard level has one icon everywhere: advisory info_outline, warning warning_amber_rounded, danger warning. Hazard colours come from SafetyColors, are fixed, and are never palette.accent or any themed colour. The backend's label is always shown with the colour (P-18, P-19).

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Every text style carries tabular figures. Switzer's default figures are already tabular and the font has no tnum feature; the theme still requests tabular figures on every role as a fallback. Numbers never set in proportional figures.

rules.name: The PHT Label Rule
rules.body: Every displayed time is Philippine Time with "PHT" shown, whatever the device's time zone. A fetch time from another PHT day names the day. The label is only dropped next to a tick whose window end already shows PHT.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: No shadows on the board. Surfaces are separated by tone and one hairline border. The one navy-tinted shadow (AppTheme.overlayShadow) is for overlays only: drawer, dialogs, snackbars, menus.

rules.name: The One Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every rule, border and divider is 1px in the hairline colour. The only other outlines are the Stale stamp (a 1.5px dash, 4px on and 3px off, in the Stale foreground colour) and the 2px focus ring.

rules.name: The Font Privacy Rule
rules.body: Every font is bundled with the app. Nothing loads a font at runtime, and no font-fetching package is a dependency (P-28).

rules.name: The Rare Motion Rule
rules.body: Animate only overlays opening and closing, expand and collapse, a newly arrived chat reply, the Updating spinner and press feedback. Never tab switches, values updating, or safety and data-state elements.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion, movement goes and only opacity changes stay, at 150ms or less. Exits are always faster than entrances.

rules.name: The Plain Curve Rule
rules.body: No ease-in, no bounce, no stagger and no scale on entrances. Entrances use the strong ease-out.

dos: Do take every colour from the palette extensions (PitchyPalette, StateColors, SafetyColors), never from literal colours in widgets.
Do show every data state as a pill with its icon and word, and keep Stale data on screen with its dashed stamp.
Do give each new weather source one fixed, cool line colour (light and dark variants) and use it only for that source's dot, rail stop and validity bar.
Do label every time PHT, and name the day when it isn't today in PHT.

Do colour an official alert only from PAGASA's own level (P-18): watch, yellow rainfall and signal 1 are advisory; advisory, orange rainfall and signals 2-3 are warning; warning, red rainfall and signals 4-5 are danger; anything else stays neutral. Always show PAGASA's words with the colour.
Do use one icon per hazard level and colour it from SafetyColors.
Do keep tap targets at least 48px, and keep cards flat with a 1px hairline border and a 12px radius.
Do set Line Board figures (rail times, kickoff time, trend axis and readout) in IBM Plex Mono digits and everything else in Switzer.
Do keep the Pitchy logo left of the screen name in every top bar.
Do make reduced motion opacity-only and no longer than 150ms, and every exit faster than its entrance.
donts: Don't theme, tint or let users customise the state colours or the safety ramp.
Don't use palette.accent or any themed colour for a hazard level.
Don't use yellow, orange or red as a source line colour, a swatch or decoration.
Don't show any state by colour alone.
Don't add shadows or elevation to cards, bars, chips or the rail; only overlays get the one navy-tinted shadow.
Don't animate tabs, values, safety or state elements, and don't use ease-in, bounce, stagger or scale.
Don't show stale, missing or unavailable data in a way that could read as Current, and don't hide it.
Don't set figures without tabular spacing.
Don't load any font at runtime or add a font-fetching package.
Don't bring the landing page's Racing Red, or any landing-page style, into the app.
Don't treat the placeholder logo as final artwork.
